prompt: Here's a NestJS `UsersService`/`UsersController` pair backing a user-profile API. Users are reporting a data-loss bug: if they PATCH only their email — sending just `{ "email": "new@x.com" }` — their previously saved `name` comes back blank afterward. Sending the full body works fine, and the loss only ever hits the field that was omitted from the PATCH payload. Walk me through the root cause in this code, explain what PUT and PATCH are each supposed to guarantee about write scope, propose a fix, and flag whether the same class of bug could hit PUT in the other direction.
